concerns.concern: There are no data points between 150 and 200 K, so the claimed drop at the Néel temperature rests on one high point at 200 K and one low point at 150 K. Dense measurements (≤5 K steps) from about 120 to 220 K are needed.
concerns.quote: There is **no data between 150 and 200 K**, i.e., across the transition itself.

concerns.concern: The size of the anomaly depends entirely on the chosen baseline. Comparing 300 K with 90 K gives about 3%, while extrapolating the high-temperature trend would give more than 5.5%. The anomaly should be defined against an explicit background model and reported with an uncertainty.
concerns.quote: The size of the anomaly therefore depends entirely on the baseline chosen.

concerns.concern: At nominally identical conditions, the room-temperature frequency and velocity differ by about 4% between Fig. 3 and Fig. 4. This is comparable to the claimed magnetic effect and implies an unaccounted systematic uncertainty.
concerns.quote: This ~4% discrepancy at nominally identical conditions is comparable to the claimed magnetic effect.

concerns.concern: Thermal contraction could tilt the sample and change the incidence angle, which shifts q and, through the strong dispersion, the measured velocity. The authors do not say how the angle was verified at each temperature.
concerns.quote: At θ = 35°, a 1° error changes sin θ, and hence q, by ~2.5%.

concerns.concern: Laser heating of the poorly heat-sunk, absorbing flake could shift the apparent transition and distort the temperature axis. Laser power and spot size are not reported, and the local temperature is not measured or estimated.
concerns.quote: Heating of tens of K would shift the apparent transition and distort the temperature axis.

concerns.concern: An adsorbed or ice layer forming on cooling could mass-load the surface and mimic softening. Vacuum conditions, reversibility on warming and hysteresis are not shown.
concerns.quote: An adsorbed or ice layer would mass-load the surface and lower the RW velocity, mimicking softening.

concerns.concern: The anomaly is not yet reproduced across several flakes, different thicknesses or repeated thermal cycles; the data appear to come from a single flake.
concerns.quote: **Reproducibility:** several NiPS₃ flakes, ideally with different thicknesses so that substrate participation varies, plus repeated thermal cycles.

concerns.concern: A substrate control is missing: the temperature dependence of the bare SiO₂/Si surface modes is not measured.
concerns.quote: **Substrate control:** the temperature dependence of the bare SiO₂/Si surface modes.

concerns.concern: There is no non-magnetic reference flake of comparable thickness (e.g. ZnPS₃ or CdPS₃) measured through the same cool-down.
concerns.quote: **Non-magnetic reference:** a flake of comparable thickness of a non-magnetic analogue (e.g., ZnPS₃ or CdPS₃)

concerns.concern: The Rayleigh wave penetrates the amorphous SiO₂, whose moduli decrease on cooling. This substrate behaviour could contribute to the temperature dependence and is not discussed.
concerns.quote: Amorphous SiO₂ has an anomalous temperature dependence: its moduli decrease on cooling.

concerns.concern: Differential thermal contraction between NiPS₃ and SiO₂/Si could impose temperature-dependent biaxial strain or cause flake slippage. This is not addressed.
concerns.quote: Differential thermal contraction between NiPS₃ and SiO₂/Si imposes temperature-dependent biaxial strain, or flake slippage.

concerns.concern: The calculated softening (0.54%) is an order of magnitude smaller than the measured value. The proposed explanations, finite temperature and the non-magnetic proxy, are speculative.
concerns.quote: The explanations offered (finite temperature, NM proxy) are speculative.

concerns.concern: The forced non-magnetic state is a poor proxy for the paramagnetic phase, since Ni²⁺ retains local moments and short-range correlations well above T_N. Disordered-local-moment or configuration-averaged calculations are needed.
concerns.quote: **NM is a poor proxy for the PM phase.**

concerns.concern: The DFT calculations use no Hubbard U for Ni 3d. Magnetostrictive quantities are sensitive to U, so results over a reasonable U range are required.
concerns.quote: Magnetostrictive quantities are sensitive to U, so results with a reasonable U range are needed.

concerns.concern: The magnetic contribution to elastic constants also involves short-range correlations through exchange-derivative and fluctuation terms. The dichotomy that optical phonons probe short-range order and acoustic phonons long-range order is therefore oversimplified.
concerns.quote: Both involve short-range correlations; this is precisely why ultrasound anomalies at magnetic transitions often track C_mag

concerns.concern: The velocity maximum near 200 K and the decrease toward T_N may already be precursor softening from 2D magnetic correlations, rather than a sharp effect of long-range order.
concerns.quote: the velocity maximum at ~200 K and the decrease toward T_N could reflect precursor softening from 2D correlations

concerns.concern: The renormalization formula using the uniform magnetic susceptibility is inappropriate for an antiferromagnet. The claim that it quantitatively links the softening to exchange striction is unsubstantiated, since no coupling constants are estimated or compared with known magnetostriction.
concerns.quote: The statement that this "quantitatively links" the softening to exchange striction is not substantiated

concerns.concern: The estimate Δc/c ≈ 2Δv/v ≈ 11% treats the heterostructure Rayleigh wave as a single medium and ignores density changes. The intrinsic modulus change would have to be larger and should be computed with the FEM model.
concerns.quote: The "Δc/c ≈ 2Δv/v ≈ 11%" estimate is misapplied.

concerns.concern: The words "giant" and "anomalous" are not justified. The effect should be compared quantitatively with established magnetoelastic systems such as transition-metal fluorides and oxides, Cr and Invar alloys.
concerns.quote: The "giant" label should be justified by comparison with established magnetoelastic systems

concerns.concern: The DFT table and the sensitivity analysis do not connect. The largest DFT change (c₆₆) barely affects the wave, and c₄₄ is unchanged, so the predicted shift comes almost entirely from c₃₃. Normalized sensitivities and the c₃₃/c₄₄ changes needed to reproduce the observation should be given.
concerns.quote: c₄₄, one of the two most sensitive constants, is identical in both phases (9.7 GPa).

concerns.concern: The simulated room-temperature frequency exceeds the measured value by about 10%, which is larger than the effect being modelled. Effective elastic constants should be fitted to the room-temperature dispersion before perturbing them.
concerns.quote: The simulated RT frequency (4.6 GHz) exceeds the measured value (4.2 GHz) by ~10%.

concerns.concern: Only one direction (q ∥ b) is tracked through the transition. Because zigzag order breaks in-plane symmetry, comparing q ∥ a with q ∥ b would be diagnostic.
concerns.quote: Zigzag order breaks in-plane symmetry, so a comparison of q ∥ a and q ∥ b would be highly diagnostic.

concerns.concern: Only one q is tracked through the transition. Full dispersions well above and below T_N are needed to invert the effective elastic constants and make the claimed c₃₃/c₄₄ decrease quantitative.
concerns.quote: Full dispersions measured well above and well below T_N would allow the effective elastic constants to be inverted.

concerns.concern: T_N is not determined independently in the same flake, for example via Raman magnon features or SHG.
concerns.quote: **Independent determination of T_N in the same flake**

concerns.concern: The low-temperature peaks are weak and broad on a sloping background. The background model in the Lorentzian fits and the origin of the error bars are not specified.
concerns.quote: Please specify the background model used in the Lorentzian fits and how the error bars were obtained.

concerns.concern: Rayleigh-wave linewidth and intensity versus temperature should be reported, since an attenuation maximum near T_N would be independent evidence of magnetoelastic coupling.
concerns.quote: an attenuation maximum near T_N would be strong independent evidence of magnetoelastic coupling.

concerns.concern: Relevant prior work is not cited or compared, including nanomechanical-resonator studies of MPS₃ membranes, spin–shear coupling in FePS₃ and the authors' own earlier BMS work. The claim that the field is "largely unexplored" is therefore inaccurate.
concerns.quote: overlooks relevant work that should be cited and compared quantitatively

concerns.concern: The Raman spectra start at about 100 cm⁻¹ and miss the low-energy Ni modes and the magnon/two-magnon region. This weakens the claim that optical phonons are an insufficient probe.
concerns.quote: This weakens the claim that optical phonons are an insufficient probe.

concerns.concern: Raman deviations from the anharmonic fits should be shown as residuals with uncertainties. Fig. 2d appears to show a step-like FWHM change near T_N inconsistent with the quoted ~0.3 cm⁻¹.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2d appears to show a step-like FWHM change near T_N that is not obviously "~0.3 cm⁻¹".

concerns.concern: The absence of the ~176 cm⁻¹ mode splitting reported in earlier work is not discussed, for example in terms of thickness, polarization geometry or resolution.
concerns.quote: The absence of the splitting reported in Ref. 25 deserves discussion

concerns.concern: The stated 1×4×2 supercell dimensions do not match that description and instead correspond to roughly 2a×2b×2c of the conventional cell.
concerns.quote: The stated "1×4×2 supercell" dimensions (11.50 × 19.91 × 12.31 Å) correspond to roughly 2a × 2b × (~2c sin β)

concerns.concern: Several computational details are missing: relaxed- versus clamped-ion elastic constants, whether the magnetic order and moments survived the strains, whether spin–orbit coupling was included, and what "four displacements" means.
concerns.quote: whether the zigzag order and moment magnitudes were preserved under the 1.5% strains

concerns.concern: At GHz frequencies, the ratio of phonon frequency to spin relaxation rate (ωτ) near T_N may matter and should be discussed.
concerns.quote: the ratio of phonon frequency to spin relaxation rate (ωτ) near T_N may matter and is worth commenting on.

concerns.concern: Only one surface mode is observed, although Sezawa modes are generally expected in a slow-on-fast system at qh ≈ 3. Their absence should be explained.
concerns.quote: In a slow-on-fast system at qh ≈ 3, Sezawa modes are generally expected. Please explain why only one mode is observed

concerns.concern: The statement that adjacent layers couple antiferromagnetically along c may be wrong; with k = [010], the interlayer stacking appears to be ferromagnetic.
concerns.quote: With k = [010] in the C-centered cell (Wildes et al., Ref. 32), the interlayer stacking is, to my understanding, ferromagnetic.

concerns.concern: The Conclusions overstate what a single-flake, single-q dataset can support.
concerns.quote: overstate what a single-flake, single-q dataset can support.

concerns.concern: The FEM methods omit the Si domain depth or use of perfectly matched layers, mesh convergence, and the material parameters and densities used.
concerns.quote: the Si domain depth, or whether perfectly matched layers were used

concerns.concern: The description of the light-scattering selection rule ("perpendicular to the propagation direction") is ambiguous. The elasto-optic contribution, relevant because NiPS₃ absorbs at 532 nm, is not discussed.
concerns.quote: "perpendicular to the propagation direction" is ambiguous.

concerns.concern: Sample characterization is incomplete: lateral flake size relative to the laser spot and acoustic wavelength, and thickness uniformity within the probed area, are not reported.
concerns.quote: Please report the thickness uniformity within the probed area, not just the "average thickness".

concerns.concern: The BMS laser power and spot size are not reported.
concerns.quote: The BMS laser power is not reported.

concerns.concern: The quoted Raman laser power of 0.024 mW seems implausibly low for high signal-to-noise. The value should be confirmed and acquisition times given.
concerns.quote: The power of 0.024 mW is very low for a "high signal-to-noise ratio".

concerns.concern: The Raman Methods state a range of 77–300 K, but the data span 90–290 K.
concerns.quote: The Methods state 77–300 K, but the data span 90–290 K.

concerns.concern: The 80 K spectrum shown in Fig. 4a is missing from the velocity plot in Fig. 4b.
concerns.quote: The 80 K spectrum in Fig. 4a does not appear in 4b.

concerns.concern: The softening is quoted inconsistently as ~5.5% and ~6%; one value with an uncertainty should be used.
concerns.quote: The softening is quoted as ~5.5% (abstract, Fig. 4) and ~6% (pp. 15, 17).

concerns.concern: The Raman assignment calls the (P₂S₆)⁴⁻ unit modes "intermolecular" where "intramolecular" is presumably meant.
concerns.quote: "Intermolecular vibrations of (P₂S₆)⁴⁻ units" should presumably be "intramolecular".

concerns.concern: The FEM Methods say "electrodynamic" where "elastodynamic" is meant.
concerns.quote: "Linear electrodynamic equation" should be "elastodynamic".

concerns.concern: The axis labels of Fig. 2a are swapped.
concerns.quote: The axis labels are swapped

concerns.concern: Fig. 4b contains a typo ("Temperaure").
concerns.quote: "Temperaure" should be "Temperature".

concerns.concern: The reference header is misspelled ("REFRENCES").
concerns.quote: "REFRENCES" should be "REFERENCES".

concerns.concern: Ref. 19 has a garbled author list.
concerns.quote: Ref. 19 has a garbled author list.

concerns.concern: The phase-velocity symbols are called "red spheres" in the text but "red circles" in the caption.
concerns.quote: called "red spheres" in the text but "red circles" in the caption.
